newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas corn 98 percent seeded versus 93 average.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas corn 98 percent seeded versus 93 average.

text.p: The Arkansas corn crop was 98 percent seeded as of Sunday, topping the five-year average of 93 percent, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop update.
The crop was rated one percent poor, 45 percent fair, 49 percent good and five percent excellent.
Soybeans were 15 percent planted, against 17 percent last year and 11 percent for the five-year average. Seven percent of the crop had emerged, compared with five percent average.
Wheat was 98 percent headed, above last year's 83 percent and the five-year average of 89 percent.
The crop was rated two percent very poor, 21 percent poor, 46 percent fair, 27 percent good and four percent excellent.
Cotton was 40 percent seeded versus the 48 percent average.
Rice was 77 percent planted, above the five-year average of 72 percent. The crop was 33 percent emerged.

"Farmers have been watching crops for problems due to excess moisture," the report said. "Black Chaff and Bacterial Stripe in wheat are being reported in many counties. Some counties reported armyworms reaching treatment thresholds."
Soil moisture was rated six percent short, 80 percent adequate and 14 percent surplus.
